facts.label: Version, perimeter and duplicate relationships
facts.text: - One registrant throughout. Every source is a report of Rocket Companies, Inc. The Q3 10-Q describes it as a holding company whose primary material assets are its equity interests in Rocket GP, LLC, Rocket LP, LLC and Redfin, with Rocket Mortgage, LLC among the entities wholly owned through Rocket Limited Partnership (Q3 10-Q page:8). Nationstar Mortgage was merged into Rocket Mortgage in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:35; Q3 10-Q page:42). - Perimeter change inside the series. The Q3 10-Q states "On July 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025, Rocket Companies completed the acquisitions of Redfin and Mr. Cooper, respectively" (Q3 10-Q page:8). The nine-month 2025 comparatives therefore hold Redfin for one quarter and no Mr. Cooper; the December 31, 2025 balance sheet holds both. The 10-K states that revenue and net income since the acquisition dates are not provided because legacy results cannot be distinguished (10-K page:165). Unaudited pro forma revenue and net income are printed for the full years 2025 and 2024 (10-K page:165) and for the third quarter and nine months of 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:19). - Up-C structure collapsed on June 30, 2025; only Class A and Class L common stock are outstanding afterwards (Q3 10-Q page:8), and Class D common shares were retired on that date (Q3 release page:7). Per-share and non-controlling-interest comparisons for 2025 cross this boundary. - Segment presentation changed. The 10-K and Q1 10-Q report two segments; from the second quarter of 2026 the company reports one segment, Mortgage, with an All Other category and prior periods recast (Q2 10-Q page:38; Q3 10-Q page:42). The Q1 release is on the old basis (Q1 release page:4); the Q2 and Q3 releases are on the new basis (Q2 release page:4; Q3 release page:3 and page:6). Fiscal 2025 segment results on the new basis are not printed; the recast covers 2025 quarters and year-to-date periods only. - Income statement presentation changed. From the first quarter of 2026 interest items were reclassified and prior-period amounts conformed (Q3 10-Q page:9 to page:10). The Q3 10-Q prints reclassified amounts for the third quarter and nine months of 2025 only. The 10-K is on the earlier captions, "Interest income, net" and "Interest and amortization expense on non-funding debt" (10-K page:136, page:103). - No source is a duplicate of another. The releases repeat figures that the 10-Qs later file, but they are separate furnished documents of earlier date and are not independent evidence of the same figures. The 10-K is the retained source for fiscal 2025 and the December 31, 2025 balances; each 10-Q repeats the December 31, 2025 balance sheet as a comparative. The Q3 release is dated October 29, 2026 and refers to a "forthcoming" Form 10-Q (Q3 release page:4); the Q3 10-Q is signed October 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:71). - Roles of issuer, borrower, guarantor and instrument. The context names no borrower, parent or guarantors. The notes state that the Senior Notes restrict "our subsidiary guarantors" but do not name them (Q3 10-Q page:31; 10-K page:177). The revolving credit agreement is listed as an exhibit with "the Guarantors party thereto" (Q3 10-Q page:71). The 10-K says Rocket Mortgage, LLC assumed the Nationstar notes that were not tendered (10-K page:165); the debt table does not label an issuer per line (Q3 10-Q page:30). The entity-by-instrument mapping is an open distinction.

facts.text: - Company-stated total liquidity: 10.1 billion at December 31, 2025, 9.4 billion at March 31, 2026, 11.2 billion at June 30, 2026 and 11.4 billion at September 30, 2026 (10-K page:121; Q1 10-Q page:59; Q2 10-Q page:64; Q3 10-Q page:67). Buy-down funds sit in cash and can be withdrawn unless a margin call has been made or a default has occurred (Q3 10-Q page:27), and margin cash held for counterparties is included in cash with an offsetting liability (Q3 10-Q page:67). Neither amount is printed. Restricted cash of 240 is outside cash (Q3 10-Q page:11). - Covenant types: minimum tangible net worth, minimum liquidity, maximum total debt or liabilities to net worth, pretax net income requirements and other customary covenants, with cross default or cross acceleration provisions in most facilities, and compliance stated at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:27). Litigation judgment thresholds are also a covenant type (10-K page:47). A money judgment above specified thresholds that is not paid, bonded or stayed could be a default under loan funding facilities (Q3 10-Q page:41). Levels, step-downs and headroom: Not supplied; the agreements are not in the pack. - Regulatory minimums at September 30, 2026: the most restrictive require net worth of approximately 3,500, liquidity of approximately 1,500 and a 6% capital ratio, with compliance stated (Q3 10-Q page:42). At December 31, 2025 fair value was 10,502 against carrying value of 10,423. Fair value fell below carrying value over the nine months while it had been above it at year end.

facts.label: Earnings quality and definition review
facts.text: - Adjusted EBITDA is net income before bond interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, share-based compensation, the change in MSR fair value from valuation assumptions (net of hedges), acquisition-related expenses, amortization of acquired intangibles, litigation accrual and other adjustments (Q3 release page:10). It includes interest on secured financing, which the company treats as a cost driven by origination volume, and excludes bond interest because it is a function of capital structure (Q3 release page:10). The Q3 10-Q states that adjusted EBITDA does not reflect interest expense or the cash needed to service debt (Q3 10-Q page:53). - Adjustments in the nine months 2026: share-based compensation 262, MSR valuation change (852) (a gain removed), acquisition-related expenses 291, amortization of acquired intangibles 338, litigation accrual 28 and other 11 (Q3 release page:8). Acquisition-related expenses of 291 recur across 2025 and 2026 (158 in nine months 2025), so the add-back is not a one-quarter item. - GAAP versus adjusted: nine months 2026 GAAP net income of 1,235 against adjusted EBITDA of 2,252. The adjusted figure removes a valuation gain on MSRs of 852 and adds back bond interest of 435, intangible amortization of 338 and acquisition costs of 291 (Q3 release page:8). - Fair value exposure: MSRs of 20,257 at fair value are the largest asset line on the balance sheet (Q3 10-Q page:4), and change in fair value of MSRs, net was a charge of 945 in the nine months 2026 against 1,128 in nine months 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:5). Sensitivity to rates and prepayment assumptions is disclosed in the fair value note (Q3 10-Q page:25 to page:26). - Servicing credit quality: delinquent loans (60-plus days past due) were 1.52% of the servicing portfolio at September 30, 2026 and 1.50% at December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:25). - Cash flow: operating cash flow is dominated by loans held for sale. Nine months 2026 disbursements of mortgage loans held for sale were (136,882) and proceeds 139,626 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Net proceeds from sales of MSRs were 1,750 in the nine months 2026 against 315 in nine months 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:7), so investing inflows from MSR sales supported liquidity. Senior note borrowings were 1,500 and repayments (1,212) in the nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Free cash flow is Not calculable on a meaningful basis for an originator that funds loans through operating cash flow.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Rocket Companies, Inc. is a Detroit-based, Delaware-incorporated holding company that originates and services US residential mortgages and, since 2025, also runs a real estate brokerage and search platform (Redfin) and personal finance businesses (Rocket Money and Rocket Loans) (Q3 10-Q page:8; 10-K page:5 to page:7). Revenue comes from four lines: gain on sale of loans, loan servicing income, interest income and other income. For the nine months of 2026 these were 3,609, 2,236, 1,640 and 1,524, summing to total revenue, net of 9,009 (Q3 10-Q page:5). The structural change in the last eighteen months is scale and mix. The June 30, 2025 Up-C Collapse removed the paired-interest structure and left only Class A and Class L common stock (10-K page:140). Redfin (July 1, 2025) and Mr. Cooper (October 1, 2025) were both bought for stock, with 1,742 and 16,973 of consideration respectively, of which cash of 252 and 3,113 repaid target debt (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:17). The servicing portfolio is now 2,007,176 of unpaid principal, of which 1,201,476 is owned MSRs and 805,700 is subservicing and other (Q3 10-Q page:62).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The mechanics that matter for a creditor are these. First, revenue durability rests on servicing fee income, which was 3,181 in the nine months of 2026 and comes from a portfolio of agency and government loans serviced under contracts that the Agencies and subservicing clients can terminate on little or no notice (Q3 10-Q page:5; 10-K page:29). Second, margin resilience depends on interest rates through both channels: higher rates cut origination (the 30-year rate rose to 7.28% by the end of September 2026 and the market was smaller than in the second quarter, Q3 10-Q page:49) but raise MSR fair value, which flatters GAAP income and is removed from adjusted measures (Q3 release page:6). Third, liquidity and refinancing run through two layers: unsecured senior notes of 10,743 and an undrawn 2,500 revolver, and secured financing of 14,187, most of which sits on uncommitted lines (CP-1). Fourth, control sits with Mr. Gilbert, whose majority voting power lets the company use controlled company exemptions from independent director requirements (10-K page:86). The company renounced certain corporate opportunities in favour of RHI II parties (10-K page:83). The governance letter agreement of March 31, 2025 with Mr. Gilbert is listed as an exhibit but its terms are not in the pack (10-K page:222).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The Up-C Collapse closed on June 30, 2025. The previously outstanding Class D common shares and Holdings LLC Units were exchanged and retired for new Class L common stock, Class B and Class C stock were eliminated, and the company now holds indirectly all voting and economic interests in Rocket Limited Partnership (10-K page:140). It was accounted for as a common control transaction. The Tax Receivable Agreement was amended so that its terms do not apply to exchanges on or after March 9, 2025, including those made in the collapse (10-K page:156). Class L shares are subject to lock-up periods, with transfers barred until the first anniversary of closing and half of the shares until the second anniversary, and all Class L shares convert automatically on the later of June 30, 2027 and the date Class L falls below the stated voting share (10-K page:90). In the third quarter of 2026, 924,439,710 Class L shares were converted into Class A shares on a one-for-one basis (Q3 10-Q page:46). The filings do not say who converted them or whether any were sold; the timing follows the first anniversary of the collapse (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The Redfin acquisition was an all-stock transaction effective July 1, 2025 with consideration of 1,742: 1,466 of Class A stock, 24 of converted equity awards and 252 of cash that settled Redfin's term loan, accrued interest and prepayment premium. Redfin carried unsecured financing of 526 at acquisition (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:17). The purchase price allocation was finalised in Q2 2026 with no measurement-period adjustments. The Mr. Cooper acquisition was an all-stock transaction effective October 1, 2025 with consideration of 16,973: 13,667 of Class A stock, 193 of converted awards and 3,113 of cash that settled Mr. Cooper's unsecured senior notes, accrued interest and fees (Q3 10-Q page:17). Liabilities assumed included secured financing of 6,461 and unsecured financing of 1,956. In Q3 2026 the allocation was finalised with a 75 increase to goodwill, arising from a 100 increase in litigation and regulatory accruals offset by a 25 decrease in net deferred tax liabilities, with no earnings impact (Q3 10-Q page:18). Goodwill from the two deals is 8,326 and 1,233 and is not tax deductible (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:18). The 10-K states that revenue and net income since the acquisition dates cannot be separated (10-K page:165).

facts.text: New debt in 2025: the note table lists 2,000 of 6.125% senior notes due 2030 and 2,000 of 6.375% senior notes due 2033 (10-K page:180), and the 2025 cash flow statement shows borrowings on senior notes of 4,000 (10-K page:138). In exchange offers, 738 of the 750 of 6.500% notes due 2029 and 955 of the 1,000 of 7.125% notes due 2032 were tendered and replaced by Rocket Companies notes, and tender offers bought 574 of 650 of 5.125% notes due 2030 and 536 of 600 of 5.750% notes due 2031. Rocket Mortgage, LLC assumed the notes not tendered. The company also redeemed 500 of 5.000% notes due 2026, 600 of 6.000% notes due 2027 and 850 of 5.500% notes due 2028 (10-K page:165 to page:166). A 364-day senior unsecured Bridge Facility is defined and its financing fees were expensed within acquisition-related expenses (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:55). The facility amount and any drawing are not printed in the pack, and it does not appear in the debt tables at either year-end or September 30, 2026.

In exchange offers, 738 of the 750 of 6.500% notes due 2029 and 955 of the 1,000 of 7.125% notes due 2032 were tendered and replaced by Rocket Companies notes, and tender offers bought 574 of 650 of 5.125% notes due 2030 and 536 of 600 of 5.750% notes due 2031. Rocket Mortgage, LLC assumed the notes not tendered. The company also redeemed 500 of 5.000% notes due 2026, 600 of 6.000% notes due 2027 and 850 of 5.500% notes due 2028 (10-K page:165 to page:166). A 364-day senior unsecured Bridge Facility is defined and its financing fees were expensed within acquisition-related expenses (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:55). The facility amount and any drawing are not printed in the pack, and it does not appear in the debt tables at either year-end or September 30, 2026.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt in 2026: on June 9, 2026 the company issued 1,500 of senior notes, of which 900 are 6.125% notes due 2031 and 600 are 6.500% notes due 2034; management said the offering was more than seven times oversubscribed and upsized from 1,200, and that proceeds redeemed outstanding senior notes and repaid other debt (Q2 release page:3, Management Language). The Q3 10-Q table shows the 2.875% notes due 2026 (1,150) redeemed at 100% plus about 6 of accrued interest, and the 5.250% notes due 2028 (62) redeemed at 100% plus about 2 of accrued interest (Q3 10-Q page:30 to page:31). The revolving credit facility was increased from 2,300 to 2,500, fully committed, and extended to July 16, 2029 (Q2 10-Q page:28; Q3 10-Q page:30). The Q2 and Q3 10-Q exhibit lists name a Revolving Credit Agreement dated July 16, 2026 with Rocket Companies, Inc. as Borrower, guarantors and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as agent (Q3 10-Q page:71), whereas the 2025 agreement had Rocket Mortgage, LLC as borrower. The filings do not say whether the 2026 agreement amends and restates the 2025 one; the change of borrower is an open distinction that matters for ranking. Nationstar Mortgage was merged into Rocket Mortgage in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:35). A personal loan funding facility was increased to 300 after September 30, 2026, and three repurchase facilities were extended and one matured after quarter end (Q3 10-Q page:29, Subsequent events). No debt transaction dated after the Q3 10-Q signature of October 30, 2026 is in the pack.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Rocket Companies, Inc. is a large but cyclical mortgage credit whose unsecured leverage looks moderate today and could weaken quickly if rates keep rising. The strongest support is a full post-acquisition earnings base: last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,843 million against senior notes of USD 10,743 million gives 3.78x gross and 2.83x net of USD 2,699 million of cash, with no note due before 2027 and an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver. The weakest point is dependence on mortgage rates, on USD 14,187 million of mostly uncommitted secured funding and on Agency servicing contracts, under a founder whose creditor-protection documents are not available. The outcome will be decided by whether adjusted revenue holds near the guided USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion without a funding or legal shock.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Rocket's unsecured leverage has fallen to a moderate level, but the improvement is earnings-led and the latest ratio is the first on a clean base. Senior notes of USD 10,743 million (principal) stand at 3.78x last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,843 million and 2.83x net of USD 2,699 million of cash, against 8.16x for FY2025 and 5.65x at March 31, 2026, when earnings held only part of the Mr. Cooper business while debt already held its assumed notes. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The ratio flatters the forward position. Adjusted revenue fell from USD 2,822 million in Q1 2026 to USD 2,761 million in Q2 2026 and USD 2,574 million in Q3 2026, and the company guides Q4 2026 to USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion, below each quarter in the last-twelve-month window. The third quarter coincided with a 30-year mortgage rate that rose from 6.43% to 7.28% and a smaller market, while GAAP net income of USD 709 million included an MSR valuation gain that the company strips out of adjusted measures. Creditors should anchor on adjusted EBITDA with that caveat and treat the 3.78x as a trailing, not forward, figure [CP-1; CP-1A].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Rocket's funding has two layers that behave differently. The unsecured layer, senior notes and an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver maturing in 2029, has no maturity before the USD 503 million convertible in April 2027, then USD 1,500 million in 2029, USD 2,076 million in 2030 and USD 2,214 million in 2031. The secured layer of USD 14,187 million sits on lines whose committed amount is USD 7,400 million, with USD 10,295 million outstanding on lines dated 2027 and USD 3,462 million on lines dated 2028. Rocket therefore faces recurring renewal and margin-call risk on warehouse capacity even though its bond maturity profile is long, and most facilities carry cross default or cross acceleration terms [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact].

Servicing fee income was USD 3,181 million in the nine months of 2026 on a portfolio of USD 2,007,176 million of unpaid principal, with 60-plus day delinquency of 1.52%. The Agencies and subservicing clients can terminate servicing with little or no notice, and MSRs of USD 20,257 million at fair value are the largest balance sheet asset and are valued with rate and prepayment assumptions. A change in Agency terms or an MSR valuation reversal would hit income, collateral value for the MSR lines and liquidity at once [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact].

Nothing in the pack shows the restricted payment, lien or guarantee terms that would limit owner actions [CP-1A governance; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on overall category].

Legal reserves rose to USD 216 million from USD 74 million, acquisition accounting added USD 100 million of litigation and regulatory accruals in Q3 2026, and a USD 175 million HouseCanary verdict against Rocket Close awaits judgment while the plaintiff is in Chapter 11. A judgment above facility thresholds that is not paid, bonded or stayed could default funding facilities, which links a legal outcome to liquidity [CP-1 claims outside funded debt; Documentary Fact].

### Version, perimeter and duplicate relationships

- One registrant throughout. Every source is a report of Rocket Companies, Inc. The Q3 10-Q describes it as a holding company whose primary material assets are its equity interests in Rocket GP, LLC, Rocket LP, LLC and Redfin, with Rocket Mortgage, LLC among the entities wholly owned through Rocket Limited Partnership (Q3 10-Q page:8). Nationstar Mortgage was merged into Rocket Mortgage in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:35; Q3 10-Q page:42).

- Perimeter change inside the series. The Q3 10-Q states "On July 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025, Rocket Companies completed the acquisitions of Redfin and Mr. Cooper, respectively" (Q3 10-Q page:8). The nine-month 2025 comparatives therefore hold Redfin for one quarter and no Mr. Cooper; the December 31, 2025 balance sheet holds both. The 10-K states that revenue and net income since the acquisition dates are not provided because legacy results cannot be distinguished (10-K page:165). Unaudited pro forma revenue and net income are printed for the full years 2025 and 2024 (10-K page:165) and for the third quarter and nine months of 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:19).

- Up-C structure collapsed on June 30, 2025; only Class A and Class L common stock are outstanding afterwards (Q3 10-Q page:8), and Class D common shares were retired on that date (Q3 release page:7). Per-share and non-controlling-interest comparisons for 2025 cross this boundary.

- Segment presentation changed. The 10-K and Q1 10-Q report two segments; from the second quarter of 2026 the company reports one segment, Mortgage, with an All Other category and prior periods recast (Q2 10-Q page:38; Q3 10-Q page:42). The Q1 release is on the old basis (Q1 release page:4); the Q2 and Q3 releases are on the new basis (Q2 release page:4; Q3 release page:3 and page:6). Fiscal 2025 segment results on the new basis are not printed; the recast covers 2025 quarters and year-to-date periods only.

- Income statement presentation changed. From the first quarter of 2026 interest items were reclassified and prior-period amounts conformed (Q3 10-Q page:9 to page:10). The Q3 10-Q prints reclassified amounts for the third quarter and nine months of 2025 only. The 10-K is on the earlier captions, "Interest income, net" and "Interest and amortization expense on non-funding debt" (10-K page:136, page:103).

- No source is a duplicate of another. The releases repeat figures that the 10-Qs later file, but they are separate furnished documents of earlier date and are not independent evidence of the same figures. The 10-K is the retained source for fiscal 2025 and the December 31, 2025 balances; each 10-Q repeats the December 31, 2025 balance sheet as a comparative. The Q3 release is dated October 29, 2026 and refers to a "forthcoming" Form 10-Q (Q3 release page:4); the Q3 10-Q is signed October 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:71).

- Roles of issuer, borrower, guarantor and instrument. The context names no borrower, parent or guarantors. The notes state that the Senior Notes restrict "our subsidiary guarantors" but do not name them (Q3 10-Q page:31; 10-K page:177). The revolving credit agreement is listed as an exhibit with "the Guarantors party thereto" (Q3 10-Q page:71). The 10-K says Rocket Mortgage, LLC assumed the Nationstar notes that were not tendered (10-K page:165); the debt table does not label an issuer per line (Q3 10-Q page:30). The entity-by-instrument mapping is an open distinction.

### Financial base view

Rocket Companies, Inc. is a Delaware holding company (Q3 10-Q page:1) whose subsidiaries originate and service US residential mortgages and run real estate and personal finance businesses (Q3 10-Q page:8). Its funded debt has two layers that must not be mixed. The first is unsecured corporate debt: senior notes with principal of 10,743 at September 30, 2026 and a revolving credit facility of 2,500 that is undrawn (Q3 10-Q page:30). The second is secured financing of 14,187: repurchase agreements, early funding facilities, MSR lines, advance facilities and personal loan lines, collateralized by loans held for sale, MSRs and advance receivables (Q3 10-Q page:27 to page:29). The company's adjusted EBITDA is stated after the interest on secured financing and before bond interest on the senior notes (Q3 release page:10), so the consistent leverage numerator is the unsecured debt. On that basis, unsecured debt of 10,743 over last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of 2,843 gives 3.78x, and 2.83x net of cash of 2,699. Both are computed here from printed components; no net debt or debt to EBITDA ratio is printed in any of the seven sources.

The direction of travel is favourable but the base is thin. The ratio on FY2025 earnings is 8.16x and on March 31, 2026 last-twelve-month earnings 5.65x, because debt already included the notes assumed from Mr. Cooper while earnings held only part of a year of that business (Mr. Cooper was acquired on October 1, 2025; Q3 10-Q page:8). Unsecured principal rose from 10,455 at December 31, 2025 to 10,743 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:30), so the improvement comes from earnings, not from debt reduction. The September 30, 2026 last-twelve-month period is the first made only of quarters that include both acquisitions.

Earnings are cyclical and rate-sensitive. Adjusted revenue was 2,822 in Q1 2026, 2,761 in Q2 2026 and 2,574 in Q3 2026, and the company guides fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted revenue to between 2.1 billion and 2.3 billion (Q3 release page:3), below each of the three 2026 quarters. The Q3 10-Q ties the quarter to a rise in the 30-year mortgage rate from 6.43% in early July to 7.28% at the end of September and a smaller mortgage market than in the second quarter (Q3 10-Q page:49). GAAP net income of 709 in Q3 2026 includes a valuation gain on MSRs that the company removes from adjusted measures (710 in the adjusted revenue reconciliation, Q3 release page:6), so GAAP and adjusted earnings tell different stories and the committee should anchor on the adjusted measures with that caveat. Last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA includes three quarters of higher adjusted revenue than the guided fourth quarter, which means the 3.78x ratio is not a forward run-rate.

Liquidity is stated by the company at 11.4 billion at September 30, 2026, made of cash of 2.7 billion, undrawn lines of credit of 2.5 billion and undrawn available MSR and advance lines of 6.2 billion (Q3 10-Q page:67). Cash of 2,699 and the undrawn revolver of 2,500 tie to the filings. The 6.2 billion does not tie to the secured financing table, which prints line amount, committed amount and outstanding balance but no availability (see Calculations). Most secured funding sits on uncommitted capacity: secured outstanding of 14,187 exceeds the committed secured line amount of 7,400 (Q3 10-Q page:29), and the 10-K flags the larger uncommitted portion of its loan funding facilities as a risk (10-K page:47). Covenants are described by type with compliance stated, and no level or headroom is printed (Q3 10-Q page:27), so covenant headroom is Not calculable.

Interest cover on a cash basis is available only for FY2025 and is mixed in basis; the quarterly reports do not print cash paid for interest. An accrual proxy, adjusted EBITDA over bond interest expense, is 4.94x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026. The confidence in this base view is Medium: statements, debt and liquidity are well sourced, while the covenant, guarantor, rating, cash-interest and secured-availability inputs that a lender would normally use to size headroom and recovery are absent from the pack.

### Liquidity, covenants and regulatory requirements

- Company-stated total liquidity: 10.1 billion at December 31, 2025, 9.4 billion at March 31, 2026, 11.2 billion at June 30, 2026 and 11.4 billion at September 30, 2026 (10-K page:121; Q1 10-Q page:59; Q2 10-Q page:64; Q3 10-Q page:67). The figures rose from 9.4 billion to 11.4 billion over the three 2026 quarters. The December 2025 figure also counts 0.1 billion of corporate cash used to self-fund loans, which later figures do not list.

- Cash is not all free. Buy-down funds sit in cash and can be withdrawn unless a margin call has been made or a default has occurred (Q3 10-Q page:27), and margin cash held for counterparties is included in cash with an offsetting liability (Q3 10-Q page:67). Neither amount is printed. Restricted cash of 240 is outside cash (Q3 10-Q page:11).

- Covenant types: minimum tangible net worth, minimum liquidity, maximum total debt or liabilities to net worth, pretax net income requirements and other customary covenants, with cross default or cross acceleration provisions in most facilities, and compliance stated at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:27). Litigation judgment thresholds are also a covenant type (10-K page:47). A money judgment above specified thresholds that is not paid, bonded or stayed could be a default under loan funding facilities (Q3 10-Q page:41). Levels, step-downs and headroom: Not supplied; the agreements are not in the pack.

- Regulatory minimums at September 30, 2026: the most restrictive require net worth of approximately 3,500, liquidity of approximately 1,500 and a 6% capital ratio, with compliance stated (Q3 10-Q page:42). These apply to Rocket Mortgage (Q3 10-Q page:42). Entity-level net worth and liquidity are not printed, so headroom against them is Not calculable; consolidated equity of 24,311 is not that measure.

- Fair value of the senior notes at September 30, 2026 was 10,258 against carrying value of 10,716, calculated from observable bond prices (Q3 10-Q page:23). At December 31, 2025 fair value was 10,502 against carrying value of 10,423. Fair value fell below carrying value over the nine months while it had been above it at year end.
### Earnings quality and definition review

- Adjusted EBITDA is net income before bond interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, share-based compensation, the change in MSR fair value from valuation assumptions (net of hedges), acquisition-related expenses, amortization of acquired intangibles, litigation accrual and other adjustments (Q3 release page:10). It includes interest on secured financing, which the company treats as a cost driven by origination volume, and excludes bond interest because it is a function of capital structure (Q3 release page:10). The Q3 10-Q states that adjusted EBITDA does not reflect interest expense or the cash needed to service debt (Q3 10-Q page:53).

- Adjustments in the nine months 2026: share-based compensation 262, MSR valuation change (852) (a gain removed), acquisition-related expenses 291, amortization of acquired intangibles 338, litigation accrual 28 and other 11 (Q3 release page:8). Acquisition-related expenses of 291 recur across 2025 and 2026 (158 in nine months 2025), so the add-back is not a one-quarter item.

- GAAP versus adjusted: nine months 2026 GAAP net income of 1,235 against adjusted EBITDA of 2,252. The adjusted figure removes a valuation gain on MSRs of 852 and adds back bond interest of 435, intangible amortization of 338 and acquisition costs of 291 (Q3 release page:8).

- Fair value exposure: MSRs of 20,257 at fair value are the largest asset line on the balance sheet (Q3 10-Q page:4), and change in fair value of MSRs, net was a charge of 945 in the nine months 2026 against 1,128 in nine months 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:5). Sensitivity to rates and prepayment assumptions is disclosed in the fair value note (Q3 10-Q page:25 to page:26).
- Servicing credit quality: delinquent loans (60-plus days past due) were 1.52% of the servicing portfolio at September 30, 2026 and 1.50% at December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:25).

- Cash flow: operating cash flow is dominated by loans held for sale. Nine months 2026 disbursements of mortgage loans held for sale were (136,882) and proceeds 139,626 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Net proceeds from sales of MSRs were 1,750 in the nine months 2026 against 315 in nine months 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:7), so investing inflows from MSR sales supported liquidity. Senior note borrowings were 1,500 and repayments (1,212) in the nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Free cash flow is Not calculable on a meaningful basis for an originator that funds loans through operating cash flow.
### Claims outside funded debt

- Operating leases: total lease liabilities of 334 at December 31, 2025, weighted average term 4.4 years (10-K page:184); not updated in the Q3 10-Q. Related party lease expense was 56 in the nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:31). Lease liabilities are outside the debt figures used here.
- Purchase commitments: 914 in aggregate at December 31, 2025, primarily over 2027 through 2030 (10-K page:122). Outside debt.

- Tax receivable agreement: 90% of realized cash tax savings payable to RHI II, LLC and Mr. Gilbert; the liability was 590 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:191). The Q3 10-Q does not print the liability amount (Q3 10-Q page:33). Outside debt.

- Legal reserves: 216 at September 30, 2026 against 74 at December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:41). A new trial verdict of 175 in damages against Rocket Close was returned on March 6, 2026 and judgment has not been entered; the plaintiff filed Chapter 11 on September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:38). The Mr. Cooper data breach class action is in class certification briefing (Q3 10-Q page:40). Acquisition accounting added 100 of litigation and regulatory accruals in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:18). Whether the 175 verdict is within the 216 reserve is not stated.

- Investor reserves for representations and warranties: 112 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:36). The maximum exposure is the outstanding principal and premium on all loans ever sold less listed exclusions, and is not quantified.

- Non-recourse MSR-related liabilities: 325 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:25). Loans subject to repurchase right from Ginnie Mae of 5,476 appear on both sides of the balance sheet (Q3 10-Q page:4).
- Asset-backed financing entities: holders of debt issued by these entities have limited to no recourse to the company (Q3 10-Q page:15).
### Perimeter, comparability and presentation

- Acquisitions: Redfin from July 1, 2025 (consideration 1,742) and Mr. Cooper from October 1, 2025 (consideration 16,973) (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:17). Nine months 2025 comparatives hold one quarter of Redfin and no Mr. Cooper. Year-on-year growth in the nine months, such as adjusted EBITDA of 2,252 against 690, therefore mixes organic change with acquired earnings. Unaudited pro forma revenue and net income for the third quarter and nine months of 2025 are printed (Q3 10-Q page:19) but no pro forma EBITDA.

- Interest captions: the 2026 income statement includes funding-facility interest in Interest expense, whereas FY2025 netted it against Interest income. For nine months 2025 the reclassification moved 246 of funding interest, 386 of deposit income and 21 of other interest (Q3 10-Q page:10). The company states that net income is unaffected; adjusted EBITDA includes secured-financing interest under its definition either way, so it should not move, but the company does not say so. Revenue, expenses and interest expense are not comparable between FY2025 as printed in the 10-K and 2026, and discrete fourth quarter 2025 revenue cannot be derived from FY2025 less nine months 2025.

- Segments: one reportable segment, Mortgage, from Q2 2026 with prior periods recast; the 10-K and Q1 10-Q use Direct to Consumer and Partner Network (Q3 10-Q page:42; 10-K page:206). Mortgage segment contribution margin was 3,572 in nine months 2026 against 1,479 in nine months 2025 (Q3 release page:4). No fiscal 2025 segment figures on the new basis are printed.

- Derived fourth quarter 2025: adjusted EBITDA of 591 (FY2025 1,281 less nine months 2025 690) and net income of 68 (FY2025 loss of 234 less nine months 2025 loss of 302). These are derived, rely on FY2025 as printed and the nine-month 2025 comparative as recast, and rest on net income being unaffected by the interest reclassification (Q3 10-Q page:10), and on adjusted EBITDA not moving, which the company does not state.

The context sets the cutoff at 2026-11-05, the current period at q3-2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-30), the prior period at fy-2025 (fiscal year ended 2025-12-31) and the reporting currency at USD. Amounts are US dollars in millions unless a cell says otherwise; the sources report in US dollars and in millions (Q3 10-Q page:5). The context file names no sponsor, parent, borrower, guarantors, ratings or research questions, and its blank fields are not read as zero. The reader question is which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to the creditor.

This module builds the fact pack from the filed sources and the two upstream handoffs. It gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion; recovery appears only as a mechanic. It uses the CP-0 readiness handoff and the CP-1 financial base handoff. It does not correct either: the figures it repeats from CP-1 (senior notes principal 10,743, secured financing 14,187, undrawn revolver 2,500, cash 2,699, leverage 3.78x gross and 2.83x net on last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of 2,843) are carried unchanged, and it adds two new source differences (the date of the 2030 and 2033 note offering and the borrower under the revolving credit agreement, see Source conflicts).

Locator convention: `<source alias> page:N`, where N is the extracted chunk number of the pinned text file, not the printed page. Aliases are defined in the first table under Sources. Category tags used in tables: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation, Insufficient Information.

### Business and transaction view

Rocket Companies, Inc. is a Detroit-based, Delaware-incorporated holding company that originates and services US residential mortgages and, since 2025, also runs a real estate brokerage and search platform (Redfin) and personal finance businesses (Rocket Money and Rocket Loans) (Q3 10-Q page:8; 10-K page:5 to page:7). Revenue comes from four lines: gain on sale of loans, loan servicing income, interest income and other income. For the nine months of 2026 these were 3,609, 2,236, 1,640 and 1,524, summing to total revenue, net of 9,009 (Q3 10-Q page:5). The structural change in the last eighteen months is scale and mix. The June 30, 2025 Up-C Collapse removed the paired-interest structure and left only Class A and Class L common stock (10-K page:140). Redfin (July 1, 2025) and Mr. Cooper (October 1, 2025) were both bought for stock, with 1,742 and 16,973 of consideration respectively, of which cash of 252 and 3,113 repaid target debt (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:17). The servicing portfolio is now 2,007,176 of unpaid principal, of which 1,201,476 is owned MSRs and 805,700 is subservicing and other (Q3 10-Q page:62).

The mechanics that matter for a creditor are these. First, revenue durability rests on servicing fee income, which was 3,181 in the nine months of 2026 and comes from a portfolio of agency and government loans serviced under contracts that the Agencies and subservicing clients can terminate on little or no notice (Q3 10-Q page:5; 10-K page:29). Second, margin resilience depends on interest rates through both channels: higher rates cut origination (the 30-year rate rose to 7.28% by the end of September 2026 and the market was smaller than in the second quarter, Q3 10-Q page:49) but raise MSR fair value, which flatters GAAP income and is removed from adjusted measures (Q3 release page:6). Third, liquidity and refinancing run through two layers: unsecured senior notes of 10,743 and an undrawn 2,500 revolver, and secured financing of 14,187, most of which sits on uncommitted lines (CP-1). Fourth, control sits with Mr. Gilbert, whose majority voting power lets the company use controlled company exemptions from independent director requirements (10-K page:86). The company renounced certain corporate opportunities in favour of RHI II parties (10-K page:83). The governance letter agreement of March 31, 2025 with Mr. Gilbert is listed as an exhibit but its terms are not in the pack (10-K page:222).

The credit-relevant history is acquisitive and equity-funded, followed by refinancing: stock paid for both targets, 4.0 billion of senior notes were raised in 2025, Mr. Cooper's legacy notes were tendered or assumed, and in 2026 1.5 billion of new notes were issued, 1,212 of notes were redeemed and a larger, longer revolver was put in place (see the transaction section). The view is Medium confidence: the documentary base for operations and transactions is strong, while the documents that would show what owners may do with cash and collateral (indentures, credit agreements, the governance letter and the proxy statement) are absent.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues
All transactions below are completed unless stated. Figures are in US dollars in millions.

The Up-C Collapse closed on June 30, 2025. The previously outstanding Class D common shares and Holdings LLC Units were exchanged and retired for new Class L common stock, Class B and Class C stock were eliminated, and the company now holds indirectly all voting and economic interests in Rocket Limited Partnership (10-K page:140). It was accounted for as a common control transaction. The Tax Receivable Agreement was amended so that its terms do not apply to exchanges on or after March 9, 2025, including those made in the collapse (10-K page:156). Class L shares are subject to lock-up periods, with transfers barred until the first anniversary of closing and half of the shares until the second anniversary, and all Class L shares convert automatically on the later of June 30, 2027 and the date Class L falls below the stated voting share (10-K page:90). In the third quarter of 2026, 924,439,710 Class L shares were converted into Class A shares on a one-for-one basis (Q3 10-Q page:46). The filings do not say who converted them or whether any were sold; the timing follows the first anniversary of the collapse (Analyst Interpretation).

The Redfin acquisition was an all-stock transaction effective July 1, 2025 with consideration of 1,742: 1,466 of Class A stock, 24 of converted equity awards and 252 of cash that settled Redfin's term loan, accrued interest and prepayment premium. Redfin carried unsecured financing of 526 at acquisition (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:17). The purchase price allocation was finalised in Q2 2026 with no measurement-period adjustments. The Mr. Cooper acquisition was an all-stock transaction effective October 1, 2025 with consideration of 16,973: 13,667 of Class A stock, 193 of converted awards and 3,113 of cash that settled Mr. Cooper's unsecured senior notes, accrued interest and fees (Q3 10-Q page:17). Liabilities assumed included secured financing of 6,461 and unsecured financing of 1,956. In Q3 2026 the allocation was finalised with a 75 increase to goodwill, arising from a 100 increase in litigation and regulatory accruals offset by a 25 decrease in net deferred tax liabilities, with no earnings impact (Q3 10-Q page:18). Goodwill from the two deals is 8,326 and 1,233 and is not tax deductible (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:18). The 10-K states that revenue and net income since the acquisition dates cannot be separated (10-K page:165).

New debt in 2025: the note table lists 2,000 of 6.125% senior notes due 2030 and 2,000 of 6.375% senior notes due 2033 (10-K page:180), and the 2025 cash flow statement shows borrowings on senior notes of 4,000 (10-K page:138). An indenture dated June 20, 2025 with guarantors named therein is listed as an exhibit (10-K page:222), and the Q3 10-Q says the 4.0 billion offering completed in June 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:67). The note table footnotes instead say the offerings were completed in October 2025 (10-K page:181). This is logged as a conflict and not reconciled. Proceeds from the June 2025 issuance were used to fund the tender, redemption and consent solicitations for Nationstar notes (10-K page:165). In exchange offers, 738 of the 750 of 6.500% notes due 2029 and 955 of the 1,000 of 7.125% notes due 2032 were tendered and replaced by Rocket Companies notes, and tender offers bought 574 of 650 of 5.125% notes due 2030 and 536 of 600 of 5.750% notes due 2031. Rocket Mortgage, LLC assumed the notes not tendered. The company also redeemed 500 of 5.000% notes due 2026, 600 of 6.000% notes due 2027 and 850 of 5.500% notes due 2028 (10-K page:165 to page:166). A 364-day senior unsecured Bridge Facility is defined and its financing fees were expensed within acquisition-related expenses (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:55). The facility amount and any drawing are not printed in the pack, and it does not appear in the debt tables at either year-end or September 30, 2026.

Other 2025 capital events: the company declared a special dividend of $0.80 per Class A share on March 10, 2025 in connection with the Up-C Collapse, paid $120.1 million on April 3, 2025 (10-K page:95). It terminated two lines of credit from RHI with capacities of 2,000 and 100 in 2025, neither drawn, and terminated a surplus debenture between RHI and RTIC (10-K page:181). A Revolving Credit Agreement dated April 30, 2025 with Rocket Mortgage, LLC as borrower and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as agent is listed in the 10-K exhibits (10-K page:222).

New debt in 2026: on June 9, 2026 the company issued 1,500 of senior notes, of which 900 are 6.125% notes due 2031 and 600 are 6.500% notes due 2034; management said the offering was more than seven times oversubscribed and upsized from 1,200, and that proceeds redeemed outstanding senior notes and repaid other debt (Q2 release page:3, Management Language). The Q3 10-Q table shows the 2.875% notes due 2026 (1,150) redeemed at 100% plus about 6 of accrued interest, and the 5.250% notes due 2028 (62) redeemed at 100% plus about 2 of accrued interest (Q3 10-Q page:30 to page:31). The revolving credit facility was increased from 2,300 to 2,500, fully committed, and extended to July 16, 2029 (Q2 10-Q page:28; Q3 10-Q page:30). The Q2 and Q3 10-Q exhibit lists name a Revolving Credit Agreement dated July 16, 2026 with Rocket Companies, Inc. as Borrower, guarantors and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as agent (Q3 10-Q page:71), whereas the 2025 agreement had Rocket Mortgage, LLC as borrower. The filings do not say whether the 2026 agreement amends and restates the 2025 one; the change of borrower is an open distinction that matters for ranking. Nationstar Mortgage was merged into Rocket Mortgage in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:35). A personal loan funding facility was increased to 300 after September 30, 2026, and three repurchase facilities were extended and one matured after quarter end (Q3 10-Q page:29, Subsequent events). No debt transaction dated after the Q3 10-Q signature of October 30, 2026 is in the pack.

Liquidity effect and status: the 2025 and 2026 issuances replaced assumed and maturing notes, lengthened the revolver and left no senior note maturing before 2027 (CP-1). Total unsecured principal rose from 10,455 at December 31, 2025 to 10,743 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:30). The 2025 special dividend and RHI line terminations show owner-related cash and backstop moves before the acquisitions; no distribution to owners appears in the 2026 cash flow statements beyond distributions to other unit holders of 8 and taxes withheld on equity awards (Q3 10-Q page:7).

### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Legal reserves rose to USD 216 million and a USD 175 million HouseCanary verdict awaits judgment. | Unpaid judgments above facility thresholds could trigger defaults; reserve coverage of the verdict is unknown. | Medium |
### Credit view

Rocket Companies, Inc. is a large but cyclical mortgage credit whose unsecured leverage looks moderate today and could weaken quickly if rates keep rising. The strongest support is a full post-acquisition earnings base: last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,843 million against senior notes of USD 10,743 million gives 3.78x gross and 2.83x net of USD 2,699 million of cash, with no note due before 2027 and an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver. The weakest point is dependence on mortgage rates, on USD 14,187 million of mostly uncommitted secured funding and on Agency servicing contracts, under a founder whose creditor-protection documents are not available. The outcome will be decided by whether adjusted revenue holds near the guided USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion without a funding or legal shock.
### Key findings

Rocket's unsecured leverage has fallen to a moderate level, but the improvement is earnings-led and the latest ratio is the first on a clean base. Senior notes of USD 10,743 million (principal) stand at 3.78x last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,843 million and 2.83x net of USD 2,699 million of cash, against 8.16x for FY2025 and 5.65x at March 31, 2026, when earnings held only part of the Mr. Cooper business while debt already held its assumed notes. Principal rose from USD 10,455 million at December 31, 2025, so deleveraging came from earnings, not repayment [CP-1 leverage table; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on cause].

The ratio flatters the forward position. Adjusted revenue fell from USD 2,822 million in Q1 2026 to USD 2,761 million in Q2 2026 and USD 2,574 million in Q3 2026, and the company guides Q4 2026 to USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion, below each quarter in the last-twelve-month window. The third quarter coincided with a 30-year mortgage rate that rose from 6.43% to 7.28% and a smaller market, while GAAP net income of USD 709 million included an MSR valuation gain that the company strips out of adjusted measures. Creditors should anchor on adjusted EBITDA with that caveat and treat the 3.78x as a trailing, not forward, figure [CP-1; CP-1A].

Rocket's funding has two layers that behave differently. The unsecured layer, senior notes and an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver maturing in 2029, has no maturity before the USD 503 million convertible in April 2027, then USD 1,500 million in 2029, USD 2,076 million in 2030 and USD 2,214 million in 2031. The secured layer of USD 14,187 million sits on lines whose committed amount is USD 7,400 million, with USD 10,295 million outstanding on lines dated 2027 and USD 3,462 million on lines dated 2028. Rocket therefore faces recurring renewal and margin-call risk on warehouse capacity even though its bond maturity profile is long, and most facilities carry cross default or cross acceleration terms [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact].

Liquidity is real but partly unverified. The company states total liquidity of USD 11.4 billion, of which only USD 2,699 million of cash and the USD 2,500 million revolver tie to the filings; the USD 6.2 billion of undrawn available MSR and advance lines cannot be reproduced from the facility table, and cash includes buy-down and margin cash that are not quantified. Stated liquidity is management data and should be attributed as such [CP-1; Management Language].

The servicing franchise is the most durable source of revenue and also a concentration. Servicing fee income was USD 3,181 million in the nine months of 2026 on a portfolio of USD 2,007,176 million of unpaid principal, with 60-plus day delinquency of 1.52%. The Agencies and subservicing clients can terminate servicing with little or no notice, and MSRs of USD 20,257 million at fair value are the largest balance sheet asset and are valued with rate and prepayment assumptions. A change in Agency terms or an MSR valuation reversal would hit income, collateral value for the MSR lines and liquidity at once [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact].

Control and sponsor behaviour matter because protections are not visible. Mr. Gilbert holds more than a majority of the voting power, the company relies on controlled company exemptions and renounces certain corporate opportunities in favour of RHI II parties. Documented capital actions are mixed: a USD 120.1 million special dividend in 2025, withdrawal of undrawn related party credit lines, equity-funded acquisitions and no distributions in the 2026 cash flow statements. Nothing in the pack shows the restricted payment, lien or guarantee terms that would limit owner actions [CP-1A governance; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on overall category].

Event risk is concentrated in litigation and acquired liabilities. Legal reserves rose to USD 216 million from USD 74 million, acquisition accounting added USD 100 million of litigation and regulatory accruals in Q3 2026, and a USD 175 million HouseCanary verdict against Rocket Close awaits judgment while the plaintiff is in Chapter 11. A judgment above facility thresholds that is not paid, bonded or stayed could default funding facilities, which links a legal outcome to liquidity [CP-1 claims outside funded debt; Documentary Fact].

Earnings carry adjustments and a definition that favours the headline. Adjusted EBITDA is after secured financing interest but before bond interest, adds back USD 291 million of acquisition-related expenses and USD 338 million of acquired intangible amortization in the nine months, and removes an MSR valuation gain of USD 852 million. Accrual cover of last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA over bond interest is 4.94x, and cash interest cover is available only for FY2025 at 2.15x on a mixed basis. Debt service capacity therefore rests on an accrual proxy and on adjusted rather than reported earnings [CP-1 earnings quality; Analyst Interpretation].

Market pricing of the unsecured notes weakened over the period. The aggregate fair value of senior notes of USD 10,258 million at September 30, 2026 was below carrying value of USD 10,716 million, whereas at December 31, 2025 fair value of USD 10,502 million was above carrying value of USD 10,423 million, and the weighted average interest rate on the notes rose to 5.43% from 5.03%. This is an aggregate, not a tranche-level price, and ratings are not supplied [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on direction].
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.

Scaled servicing and origination franchise [Documentary Fact]. Rocket Companies, Inc. services USD 2,007,176 million of unpaid principal, earned USD 3,181 million of servicing fee income in the nine months of 2026 and closed USD 43.6 billion of loans in Q3 2026. Recurring servicing fees support revenue visibility through a rate cycle better than origination alone, and the portfolio's 60-plus day delinquency of 1.52% is stable against 1.50% at year end [CP-1A operating model].

Moderate unsecured leverage on a full earnings base [Documentary Fact]. Gross 3.78x and net 2.83x on last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, with accrual bond interest cover of 4.94x, give room to absorb some earnings decline before leverage reaches the 5.65x seen at March 31, 2026 [CP-1 leverage table; Analyst Interpretation on headroom].

Long unsecured maturity profile and an undrawn revolver [Documentary Fact]. No note matures before April 2027, the largest annual maturities fall in 2031 and 2033, and the USD 2,500 million revolver is undrawn and runs to 2029, which gives the issuer time and a committed buffer [CP-1 debt maturities; CP-1 liquidity table].

Equity-funded growth [Documentary Fact]. Redfin and Mr. Cooper were bought for stock, with cash of USD 252 million and USD 3,113 million used to settle target debt, so the acquisitions did not require a new debt-funded purchase price. Equity of USD 24,311 million and equity less goodwill and intangibles of USD 11,745 million (a consolidated proxy, not a covenant measure) provide loss-absorbing capital for the debt [CP-1A transactions; CP-1 financials].

Stated compliance [Documentary Fact]. The company states compliance with all funding covenants and with agency net worth, liquidity and capital ratio requirements at September 30, 2026. This is a statement, not a measured headroom [CP-1].
Weaknesses.

Rate-sensitive, cyclical earnings [Documentary Fact]. Gain on sale margin was 2.54% in Q3 2026 against 2.80% a year earlier, adjusted revenue has fallen each quarter of 2026, and fourth-quarter adjusted revenue is guided to USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion. Rising rates reduce origination volume while raising MSR value, so earnings quality depends on valuation items the company excludes from adjusted measures [CP-1; CP-1A].

Uncommitted secured funding and renewal risk [Documentary Fact]. Secured financing of USD 14,187 million exceeds the USD 7,400 million committed secured lines, almost all of it matures in 2027 and 2028, and most facilities have cross default terms. A margin call or non-renewal would draw on cash first [CP-1 debt stack].

Agency and counterparty dependence [Documentary Fact]. Servicing and loan sales depend on Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae programmes and guidelines, and counterparties can terminate servicing. The loss of eligibility or fee cuts would hit income and MSR collateral together [CP-1A operating model].

Founder control with unseen protections [Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on protective terms]. The controlling holder, controlled company exemptions and renounced corporate opportunities limit board-level checks, and the governance letter, indentures and credit agreements that would limit owner actions are not supplied. This is a monitoring weakness, not evidence of owner extraction [CP-1A ownership and governance].

Legal and acquired-liability exposure [Documentary Fact]. Reserves of USD 216 million, a USD 175 million verdict awaiting judgment, a data breach class action inherited from Mr. Cooper and unquantified investor representation exposure form event risk that could reach liquidity through judgment thresholds [CP-1 claims outside funded debt].

Opaque debt terms and liquidity [Insufficient Information]. Covenant levels, guarantor names, per-instrument issuer roles, ratings, cash paid for interest in 2026 and the basis of USD 6.2 billion of stated secured availability are not supplied, so headroom, ranking and cash cover cannot be sized. Missing evidence is not read as adverse; it limits confidence [CP-0; CP-1; CP-1A].

Comparability and adjustments [Analyst Interpretation]. Perimeter changes, a segment recast, interest caption changes and large add-backs mean year-on-year growth mixes acquired and organic change, and revenue cannot be compared between FY2025 and 2026 captions. Credit judgments should rest on net income, adjusted EBITDA and balance sheet figures [CP-0; CP-1].
### Assessment and thesis
| Item | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | A scaled, rate-sensitive mortgage originator and servicer with moderate unsecured leverage on a full post-acquisition earnings base, supported by cash and an undrawn revolver, but exposed to uncommitted secured funding, Agency dependence, litigation event risk and founder control whose creditor protections are unseen. Fundamental view: moderate and cyclical, not a rating | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and debt stack figures; CP-1A operating model, ownership, governance and conflicts |

| Thesis | Rocket Companies, Inc.'s unsecured creditors are supported by a large servicing franchise and moderate trailing leverage, but the credit depends on mortgage rates, warehouse renewals and documents that are not yet in view. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Strengths and weaknesses above |
The confidence is Medium, not High, because CP-1A judged CP-2 READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and the inherited source limitations include missing covenant, guarantor, rating and cash interest inputs.
